title: North Dakota AI Laws

reading.body:
North Dakota's only AI-related law is a political-speech disclosure rule, not a rule about data centers, power, or model development.

The law, HB1167, passed on 2025-04-11. It requires a prominent disclaimer on political communications and advertising that use digital content created in whole or in part with artificial intelligence to visually or audibly impersonate a human. It exempts AI used for text generation, grammar, spelling, stylistic editing, or enhancing existing content without creating a new impersonation, and it defines artificial intelligence for that purpose.

That scope matters for anyone reading state AI law as a signal about compute. This statute governs a narrow category of synthetic media in elections. It says nothing about siting, interconnection, electricity procurement, or the physical buildout that constrains AI scaling. A state can regulate an AI output while regulating none of the inputs.

The data covers one law and its enrolled text. It does not show whether other AI-related bills were introduced and failed, what agencies enforce the requirement, or what penalties apply. One enacted law is a count, not a measure of a state's posture, and it should not be read as one.

Enacted AI laws in North Dakota

1 law this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • HB1167: Artificial intelligence disclosure statements. passed 2025-04-11

    This North Dakota law requires a prominent disclaimer on political communications and advertising that contain digital content created in whole or in part with artificial intelligence to visually or audibly impersonate a human. It exempts certain uses of artificial intelligence for text generation, grammar, spelling, stylistic editing, or enhancing existing content without creating a new impersonation. It defines artificial intelligence for this purpose.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for North Dakota. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
